subject: Audit Trail Delivery: retention tiers, export formats and tamper-proofing
messages:
From: Ronald Price <ronald.price@heliumbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: ServCo Security Team <security@servco.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit trails - delivery formats and tamper evidence

Jordan —

Thanks for the briefing last week. As we scope procurement and the downstream compliance controls, we need a concise response to the following items for our internal RFP:  

1) Retention tiers: for audit logs (auth, admin, system events, inference request metadata) — what default retention windows do you offer for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Is tiering configurable per-tenant/route?
2) Export formats & bulk delivery: what formats can you deliver for forensics (JSONL, NDJSON, Parquet, CSV), and do exports include KV-cache traces or only request/response metadata? What is throughput and estimated time for a 1TB export?
3) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody: do exports carry signed manifests or checksums? Do you provide signed timestamps or notarization options?
4) Live slicing / partial extracts: can we request time-range + filter (user_id, model, route) exports? Are there API endpoints and are they rate-limited?

We'd like a short, authoritative reply we can attach to the RFP packet. If you can attach a sample export schema and an estimated SLA for delivery, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Ronald
Senior Manager, Compliance
Helium Bank

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Ronald —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers inline below; attaching a one-page export spec and a retention-tier matrix for convenience (see attachments). We'll follow up with timing/throughput numbers for a 1TB bulk extract once Ben has had a chance to estimate from our export service.

1) Retention tiers
- Hosted: default 90 days for request/response metadata, 365 days for auth and admin events (can be shortened to meet privacy requests).
- Dedicated: default 365 days for most audit events; customers can request longer retention on a per-contract basis (multi-year available).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention is controlled by the customer; Redwood ships tooling and configuration templates.
- Tiering: yes — per-tenant and per-route retention overrides are supported in Dedicated and Hosted (via Admin API flags); Private gives full control.

2) Export formats & bulk delivery
- Formats: NDJSON (default), JSONL, Parquet (columnar for large-scale analytics), CSV (summary exports).
- Contents: exports include request metadata, response metadata, auth/admin events, and optional verbatim request/response payloads. KV-cache internal traces are excluded from standard forensic exports; we can provide enriched session traces as a separate, time-limited export for forensic teams upon request.
- Throughput/1TB estimate: typical streaming export throughput is 50-150 MB/s depending on destination (S3 vs secure FTP) and compression. For a 1TB NDJSON export pushed to S3 the ballpark is 2–6 hours; we'll provide a formal ETA after confirming region and egress path.

3) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody
- Checksums: all bulk exports are delivered with SHA-256 manifests.
- Signed manifests: for Dedicated and Hosted Enterprise tiers we provide GPG-signed manifests; Private deployments can enable HSM-based signing.
- Timestamps & notarization: we provide ISO-8601 timestamps and can optionally include signed timestamping via a third-party TSA (additional cost/time).

4) Live slicing / partial extracts
- API: yes — we expose an export API that accepts time-range, user_id, model_id, route, and event_type filters.
- Rate limits: export jobs are queued; there are per-account concurrency limits (default 3 concurrent jobs). For large slices we recommend offline bulk export endpoints to avoid impacting serving latency.

Deliverables attached: small export schema (PDF) and retention-tier matrix (XLSX). I'll loop Ben for throughput numbers and Kimberly for legal/chain-of-custody notes.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

Team —

Answers below, and I've attached a short Q&A PDF and the signed RFI acknowledgement. Ben included a conservative throughput estimate and Marissa added notes on delivery SLA and packaging.

- Redaction: We support server-side redaction rules at export time (PII scrubbing based on regex and schema-mapped fields). Exports can be produced in both redacted and unredacted variants; redacted exports are marked in the manifest and carry a redaction-summary file.

- GPG-signed manifests and key rotation: Redwood publishes a rotating GPG verification key; signatures use the current key and every manifest includes the key ID and a rotation history pointer. Rotation is documented in the manifest change-log. We also support verifying signatures via our public key hub (link in the attached Q&A).

- HSM-signed exports in Private: HSM key material is customer-managed for Private deployments; Redwood will assist with signing workflows but key provenance/assertions remain under customer control (we provide an attestable signing wrapper and sample audits).

Delivery SLA / throughput (Ben)
- Export SLA for Enterprise Hosted/Dedicated: 48–72 hour SLA for scheduled bulk exports (1TB class) after request acceptance. Urgent expedited jobs available as an add-on.
- Throughput: conservative baseline 75 MB/s compressed streaming to S3 in-region; 1TB ~ 3.5 hours compressed (region/egress dependent).

Packaging & chain-of-custody (Marissa)
- Delivery artifacts: data files (NDJSON/Parquet), manifest.sha256, manifest.sig.gpg, redaction-summary.json (if redacted), and a signed acknowledgement PDF (signed-rfi-ack.pdf).
- Chain-of-custody: we timestamp job creation and delivery events and record them to an append-only audit ledger; ledger entries are available as part of the export bundle for forensic review.

Next steps: attaching the Q&A and the export spec. If this is sufficient, we'll mark this RFP question as answered and provide the signed acknowledgement for your packet. If Helium Bank would like the TSA notarization option or HSM provisioning, we can scope that as add-ons and return pricing.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
